card.band: 8 h. The levers are quantizer design, LPC order, long-term prediction and entropy coding. Partial credit is dense. A frontier agent improves beyond the baseline but is below the reference. A weaker model barely matches the baseline.
card.cheat: A rate cap on real bytes prevents out-of-band side channels. Decoding runs in a clean container with no access to the evaluation audio.
card.grading: The agent's codec runs on hidden utterances from the other-condition split and other speakers. Scored by SNR plus log-spectral distance averaged over three bitrates, with a rate cap checked on actual bytes. Normalised between the shipped baseline and our reference.
card.reference: Our own LPC plus rANS codec with noise shaping, tuned on the training subset. It reaches a reported gain over the baseline.
card.source: https://www.openslr.org/12/ (LibriSpeech, CC BY 4.0); Opus (BSD) as the baseline
card.task: /app ships train-clean-100 subsets, an evaluation harness and a baseline (mu-law/ADPCM plus an Opus-style mode). The agent designs an encoder and decoder (LPC or noise-feedback coding, entropy coding, or a small CPU-trained learned codec) for a fixed bitrate set, and delivers an encode/decode CLI.
card.title: Speech codec rate-distortion on LibriSpeech under a CPU budget

source_notes: Subsets sizes (page): dev-clean 337M, test-clean 346M, test-other 328M, train-clean-100 6.3G (100 h), whole corpus ~1000 h 16 kHz. Opus README: no objective-quality numbers; Codec2 README: 700-3200 bit/s, no PESQ/MOS numbers; opus_demo has -cbr -complexity options. OOD: tune on train-clean-100 speakers, hidden = test-other (noisier) or different language/instrument data not in LibriSpeech. INFERRED run time per eval on 8 CPUs: 200 utterances (~30 min audio) encode+decode with Opus <30 s; a pure-Python/numpy LPC codec ~1-3 min; training a small conv/GRU codec on 10 h of audio ~1-3 h. Levers: LPC order, quantizer design, entropy coding (rANS), noise shaping, long-term prediction.
source_version: Baseline: mu-law / ADPCM or Opus via opus_demo at a fixed bitrate, decoded and scored on a held-out set -> Reference: our own better codec, e.g. LPC/noise-feedback or small learned (CPU-trained) codec reaching higher quality at the same bitrate, or Opus at higher complexity setting

facts.claim: LibriSpeech test-other is a separate download (328M) and train-clean-100 is 6.3G (100 h); corpus is about 1000 h of 16 kHz read English

Opus release v1.5.2 exists (minor maintenance release, April 2024)

Opus licence is BSD-style (redistribution in source and binary form permitted) with a royalty-free patent licence; COPYING does not literally name BSD-3-Clause and its non-endorsement clause names IETF/ISOC
Opus SILK layer uses LPC, optional long-term (pitch) prediction, noise shaping (encoder side) and a range coder, so the seed's levers already exist in the baseline's public design (RFC 6716)
Our LPC+rANS reference codec reaches a reported gain over the baseline (no number given in the seed)

spike_plan.kill_if: Opus cannot be built offline after one repair attempt (then the baseline must drop to mu-law/ADPCM only); or a naive LPC prototype already matches the reference-level gain (K8); or the metric is non-deterministic across runs.
spike_plan.pass_if: Opus builds offline and is deterministic; the LPC prototype gives a dense, non-trivial spread of SNR/LSD across bitrates and orders; baseline is clearly beatable but not trivially beaten.
steps: In a throwaway networked Linux container, fetch xiph/opus at v1.5.2 (5f74436 per seed) and run meson setup and compile with the system meson; record the exact failure behind the red probe (fetch_ok false vs clone_ok true is contradictory).
Once Opus builds, build opus_demo and encode/decode 20 train-clean-100 utterances at three CBR bitrates; compute SNR and LSD per file with a short script.
Run the same encode/decode twice and diff the bytes and decoded PCM to confirm determinism.
Write a quick LPC (order 16) plus uniform quantizer with ideal entropy-estimated bytes; sweep order and step size to see whether SNR and LSD move smoothly at matched bytes against Opus.
Check that the rate cap on actual bytes is measurable and that a naive LPC coder does not already beat Opus on both metrics at all three bitrates (that would signal K8).

v1.summary: The seed is a research-class speech codec task on LibriSpeech with a real, permissively licensed Opus baseline and a private reference; no gate fails, but the Opus offline build is red and the reference gain is unquantified, so the spike must first repair the baseline build. The main risk is that the target design (LPC, LTP, noise shaping, range coding) is already public in SILK/RFC 6716, which the 8 h band estimate does not account for.

v2.note: Weakest survivor. The reference is unbuilt and its gain unquantified. The Opus build probe was red. SNR plus LSD rewards waveform matching, so a perceptual Opus baseline is easy to beat on SNR and the baseline-to-reference scale is uncalibrated. test-other is a weak OOD shift. Before investing, build the reference and measure the spread against mu-law/ADPCM.
